# ArkhamPad Learn: full text


# What Is Elysium? Kinetiq's Hyperliquid Layer 2 Explained
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/what-is-elysium/

Elysium is a Layer 2 blockchain for the Hyperliquid ecosystem, built by Kinetiq, the team behind kHYPE liquid staking. It is an Arbitrum Orbit chain that settles to HyperEVM, runs standard EVM contracts and wallets, and uses HYPE as its gas token. It exists to give trading apps, launchpads and AMMs far more block space than HyperEVM offers.

## What is Elysium in simple terms?

Elysium is a separate blockchain that sits on top of HyperEVM, the smart contract chain of Hyperliquid. This kind of chain is called a Layer 2 (L2): it produces its own blocks and processes its own transactions, but it settles back to a base chain. For Elysium, that base chain is HyperEVM.

Elysium was built by Kinetiq, the team known for kHYPE, a liquid staking token for HYPE. The chain is operated with Conduit, an infrastructure provider that runs rollup chains.

For a user, Elysium feels like any other EVM network. You add it to a wallet, hold some HYPE for gas, and use apps. The difference is speed and room. Elysium is designed for very fast blocks, with a target of 100 to 200 milliseconds, and much higher throughput than its base layer.

## Why does Hyperliquid need a Layer 2?

Hyperliquid keeps HyperEVM blocks small on purpose. That choice keeps the base layer lean, but it limits how many transactions apps can push through at once.

Some apps need a lot of block space. Trading interfaces, token launchpads and AMMs (automated market makers, the pools that let you swap one token for another) all create many transactions, and demand spikes when many people trade at the same moment.

Elysium gives those apps their own lane. Activity on Elysium does not compete for space in HyperEVM blocks. HyperEVM only receives compact records that let the L2 settle. For a side-by-side comparison of the two chains, read [Elysium vs HyperEVM](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-vs-hyperevm/).

## How does Elysium work under the hood?

Elysium is an Arbitrum Orbit chain. Orbit is the framework for launching chains on the Arbitrum Nitro stack and ArbOS, the operating layer of Arbitrum chains. Because the stack is standard, Elysium is fully EVM compatible. Solidity contracts deploy unchanged, and normal tools and wallets such as MetaMask work as they do elsewhere.

Four parts are worth knowing:

- **Sequencer.** One sequencer orders transactions at launch. It sorts them by priority fee, and there is no public mempool where pending transactions wait in view.
- **Data availability.** An AnyTrust-style committee stores the full transaction data and posts compact certificates to HyperEVM. If the committee cannot do its job, the chain falls back to posting full data on HyperEVM.
- **Validators.** Validators are permissioned at launch. Permissionless fraud proofs, through Arbitrum's BoLD system, are planned for later.
- **Escape hatch.** If the sequencer ever refuses your transaction, you can force-include it through the delayed inbox on HyperEVM.

The design is optimistic. The chain treats posted results as correct unless someone challenges them within a set window. That window is why withdrawals through the official bridge take time, as explained in [Elysium withdrawal time](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-withdrawal-time/).

## What token does Elysium use for gas?

Elysium uses HYPE, Hyperliquid's native token, as its gas token. HYPE is bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM, so there is no new coin to buy just to pay fees. Gas costs on Elysium are very low, but you still need a small HYPE balance to send any transaction. [HYPE on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/hype-on-elysium/) covers how HYPE moves between chains and how it is used for trading.

There is no Elysium token at this time, and there is no official points program. Be careful with anyone selling an "Elysium token" or promising points. One related fact: half of Elysium sequencer fees are earmarked for open-market buybacks of KNTQ, the Kinetiq token.

## Elysium mainnet: chain ID and launch date

The key network details:

- Network: Elysium mainnet
- Chain ID: 99901
- Gas token: HYPE
- Settles to: HyperEVM (chain ID 999)
- Public mainnet launch date announced by Kinetiq: November 9, 2026

Some features come after launch. Kinetiq plans an ArbOS upgrade about a month after mainnet that would let smart contracts read live HyperCore market data and route orders to HyperCore, the trading engine at the center of Hyperliquid. That upgrade is not live at launch. For a trader's view of the launch period, read [Elysium mainnet launch](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-mainnet-launch/).

## What can you do on Elysium?

Most early activity on Elysium is trading and launching tokens. People swap HYPE for new tokens, many of them memecoins, and create tokens of their own.

ArkhamPad is a launchpad and trading site built for this. Its [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/) lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium from every launchpad, with market cap, volume, holders and live trades in one place. You can trade any of them from a single token page.

You can also launch your own coin. On ArkhamPad it takes about 30 seconds, and the whole supply goes into a pool with liquidity locked forever. The steps are in [create a token on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/create-a-token-on-elysium/).

Memecoins are high risk. Prices can move sharply within minutes, and many tokens fall to near zero. Only use money you can afford to lose.

## How do you get started on Elysium?

1. Get a wallet. On ArkhamPad you can log in with email or Google and an embedded wallet is created for you, or you can connect a wallet you already use.
2. Fund it. Bridge HYPE from HyperEVM on the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/), or bring USDC from Base, which is converted to HYPE on the way in.
3. Keep a little HYPE for gas, then explore tokens or launch one.

Deposits arrive within seconds to a few minutes. Moving funds back to HyperEVM through the official bridge takes about 5.5 days, so plan your exits ahead of time.

## FAQ

**Is Elysium a Layer 2 or a sidechain?**
Elysium is a Layer 2. It is an Arbitrum Orbit chain that settles to HyperEVM and uses an optimistic design: results are treated as valid unless challenged within a set period. Transaction data is held by an AnyTrust-style committee that posts compact certificates to HyperEVM, with a fallback to full data. Validators are permissioned at launch, and permissionless fraud proofs are planned for later.

**Who built Elysium?**
Elysium was built by Kinetiq, the team behind kHYPE, a liquid staking token for HYPE. The chain is operated with Conduit, an infrastructure provider for rollup chains. Elysium belongs to the Hyperliquid ecosystem and settles to HyperEVM, Hyperliquid's smart contract layer, rather than to Ethereum.

**Does Elysium have its own token or airdrop?**
No. There is no Elysium token and no official points program at this time. Gas is paid in HYPE. Half of Elysium sequencer fees are earmarked for open-market buybacks of KNTQ, Kinetiq's token. Treat any offer of an Elysium token, presale or points claim as a likely scam unless Kinetiq announces it through its official channels.

**What is the Elysium chain ID?**
The Elysium mainnet chain ID is 99901. HyperEVM, the chain Elysium settles to, uses chain ID 999. If you add Elysium to a wallet by hand, check the chain ID carefully and take network details only from official sources, because a wrong setting can point your wallet at a different network.

**Can I use MetaMask on Elysium?**
Yes. Elysium runs the standard Arbitrum Nitro stack, so it is fully EVM compatible. MetaMask and other common EVM wallets work once the network is added. You need some HYPE in the wallet to pay gas. If you prefer not to manage a wallet extension, ArkhamPad also supports email or Google login with an embedded wallet.


# Elysium vs HyperEVM: What's the Difference?
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-vs-hyperevm/

HyperEVM is Hyperliquid's own smart contract chain (chain ID 999), and it keeps its blocks small on purpose. Elysium (chain ID 99901) is a Layer 2 built by Kinetiq that settles to HyperEVM and offers much more block space and very fast blocks for trading apps. Both are EVM chains and both use HYPE for gas.

## What is HyperEVM?

HyperEVM is the EVM smart contract layer of Hyperliquid. It is part of Hyperliquid's base network, alongside HyperCore, the trading engine behind Hyperliquid's markets. HYPE is its native token and its chain ID is 999.

Hyperliquid keeps HyperEVM blocks small on purpose. That protects the base layer, but it caps how much activity apps can fit into each block. For most transfers and everyday contract calls this is fine. For apps that generate a constant stream of trades, it becomes a limit.

## What is Elysium, and how does it relate to HyperEVM?

Elysium is a Layer 2 built by Kinetiq. It runs its own blocks and settles to HyperEVM, the way many Ethereum Layer 2s settle to Ethereum. It is an Arbitrum Orbit chain, so it uses the standard Arbitrum Nitro stack and ArbOS. The full background is in [what is Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/what-is-elysium/).

The relationship is simple. HyperEVM is the base. Elysium is an extra lane built on top of it for busy trading apps, launchpads and AMMs.

## Elysium vs HyperEVM: the key differences

- **Layer.** HyperEVM is part of Hyperliquid's base network. Elysium is a Layer 2 that settles to HyperEVM.
- **Block space.** HyperEVM blocks are small by design. Elysium is built for much more block space and high throughput.
- **Block speed.** Elysium targets very fast blocks, in the range of 100 to 200 milliseconds.
- **Gas token.** Both use HYPE. On Elysium it is HYPE bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM.
- **Chain ID.** HyperEVM is 999. Elysium mainnet is 99901.
- **Compatibility.** Both are EVM chains. Solidity contracts and common wallets work on both.
- **Transaction ordering.** On Elysium at launch, a single sequencer orders transactions by priority fee, with no public mempool.
- **Exits.** Leaving Elysium through the official bridge takes about 5.5 days. Moving into Elysium takes seconds to a few minutes.

## Is Elysium as secure as HyperEVM?

They use different trust models, and it helps to know where the trust sits.

On Elysium, one sequencer orders transactions at launch. Validators are permissioned, which means only approved parties can post and check results for now. Permissionless fraud proofs, through Arbitrum's BoLD system, are planned for later, which would let anyone challenge an invalid result.

Two protections exist from day one. First, if the sequencer refuses your transaction, you can force-include it through the delayed inbox on HyperEVM. Second, the data needed to rebuild the chain is stored by an AnyTrust-style committee that posts compact certificates to HyperEVM, with a fallback to posting full data on HyperEVM.

The optimistic design also explains the exit delay. Withdrawals wait for a challenge period so any invalid result can be disputed first. The details are in [Elysium withdrawal time](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-withdrawal-time/).

## How do you move funds between HyperEVM and Elysium?

Deposits go from HyperEVM to Elysium through the official Elysium bridge and arrive within seconds to a few minutes. Your HYPE arrives 1:1. You can start from the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/), and the full walkthrough is in [bridge HYPE to Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/bridge-hype-to-elysium/).

If your funds are on Base instead, ArkhamPad also accepts USDC from Base and converts it to HYPE on the way in, so you land on Elysium ready to trade. See [buy Elysium tokens with USDC](https://arkhampad.com/learn/buy-elysium-tokens-with-usdc/).

Withdrawals back to HyperEVM through the official bridge take about 5.5 days (around 132 hours) on mainnet. ArkhamPad is working on a faster exit route, but there is no date yet.

## Which chain should you use?

It depends on what you want to do.

- **Trading new Elysium tokens or launching a coin:** Elysium. That is where those tokens and pools live, and the extra block space is built for frequent trading.
- **Using apps that only exist on HyperEVM:** HyperEVM. Contracts and balances are separate per chain.
- **Funds you may need quickly:** think before bridging. Getting in is fast. Getting out through the official bridge takes about 5.5 days.

Fees are another factor. Gas on Elysium is very low, but trading costs include more than gas. [Elysium gas fees](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-gas-fees/) breaks down what a trade really costs.

## What changes after the planned HyperCore upgrade?

Kinetiq plans an ArbOS upgrade about a month after Elysium mainnet. It would let smart contracts on Elysium read live HyperCore market data and route orders to HyperCore.

That would connect Elysium more closely to the rest of Hyperliquid. Apps on Elysium could use live market data from HyperCore inside their contracts. This upgrade is not live at launch, so treat it as planned until it ships.

## FAQ

**Is Elysium faster than HyperEVM?**
Elysium is designed for very fast blocks, with a target of 100 to 200 milliseconds, and for much higher throughput. HyperEVM keeps its blocks small on purpose. For apps that send many transactions, such as launchpads and trading sites, Elysium offers far more room. Keep in mind that the block time is a design target, and real conditions can vary.

**Do I need a different token for gas on Elysium?**
No. Both Elysium and HyperEVM use HYPE for gas. On Elysium, HYPE is bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM through the official bridge, so there is no separate gas token to buy. Keep a small amount of HYPE on Elysium at all times, because every transaction, including selling a token, needs some gas.

**Can I use the same wallet address on Elysium and HyperEVM?**
Yes. Both are EVM chains, so a normal EVM wallet address works on both. Balances are separate, though. HYPE on HyperEVM does not show up on Elysium until you bridge it, and tokens bought on Elysium stay on Elysium. Always check which network your wallet is connected to before you send funds.

**Why does leaving Elysium take longer than entering it?**
Elysium is an optimistic Layer 2. Deposits from HyperEVM arrive within seconds to a few minutes. Withdrawals through the official bridge must wait for a challenge period, currently about 5.5 days on mainnet, so that any invalid result can be disputed before funds are released on HyperEVM.

**Are tokens on HyperEVM automatically available on Elysium?**
No. Each chain has its own contracts and balances. A token deployed on HyperEVM does not appear on Elysium by itself, and a token launched on Elysium lives only on Elysium. To use HYPE on Elysium, you bridge it through the official Elysium bridge, where it arrives 1:1.


# HYPE on Elysium: Gas, Trading and Bridging Explained
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/hype-on-elysium/

On Elysium, HYPE is both the gas token and the main trading currency. It is bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM through the official Elysium bridge, arrives within seconds to a few minutes, and pays for every transaction. Most Elysium tokens trade against HYPE, so HYPE is what you spend to buy and what you receive when you sell.

## What is HYPE and why does Elysium use it?

HYPE is the native token of Hyperliquid. It pays gas on HyperEVM, Hyperliquid's smart contract chain.

Elysium, the Layer 2 built by Kinetiq on top of HyperEVM, uses HYPE as its gas token too. This was a deliberate choice: users do not need a new token just to pay fees. If you already hold HYPE, you already hold what Elysium needs.

HYPE plays two roles on Elysium:

- **Gas.** Every transaction pays a small network fee in HYPE.
- **Trading currency.** Most tokens on Elysium are paired with HYPE, so prices and market caps are measured in HYPE.

## How do you get HYPE onto Elysium?

The standard route is the official Elysium bridge. You deposit HYPE on HyperEVM and the same amount becomes available on Elysium. It is a 1:1 bridge with no conversion. Deposits arrive within seconds to a few minutes.

On ArkhamPad you can start this from the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/). Each step is shown in [bridge HYPE to Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/bridge-hype-to-elysium/).

If you do not hold HYPE yet, there is a second route. ArkhamPad accepts USDC from Base and converts it to HYPE on the way in through a cross-chain route, so you arrive on Elysium holding HYPE. That process is covered in [buy Elysium tokens with USDC](https://arkhampad.com/learn/buy-elysium-tokens-with-usdc/).

## How does HYPE pay for gas on Elysium?

Every action on Elysium is a transaction: buying a token, selling, approving, creating a coin or bridging out. Each one pays a network fee in HYPE, taken from your balance.

Gas costs on Elysium are very low, so this fee is usually a tiny part of a trade. It still matters in one situation. If you spend all your HYPE on a token, you will have nothing left to pay gas when you want to sell. Always leave a small reserve of HYPE in your wallet after each buy.

At launch, one sequencer orders Elysium transactions by priority fee. In practice this means a higher priority fee can place a transaction earlier in the queue. For a full cost breakdown, see [Elysium gas fees](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-gas-fees/).

## Why do Elysium tokens trade against HYPE?

Most tokens on Elysium are paired with HYPE. The Discover page on ArkhamPad lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium, from every launchpad, with market cap, 24h change, volume and holders shown in HYPE terms.

Under the hood, pools hold wrapped HYPE. Wrapped HYPE is a token-standard version of HYPE that smart contracts and pools can hold like any other token. When you trade through ArkhamPad you do not need to wrap anything yourself: you pay HYPE and receive tokens, or sell tokens and receive HYPE. The ArkhamPad router is a single smart contract that trades both Uniswap v3 style and v4 style pools, so one buy box works for any Elysium token.

Pricing in HYPE has a side effect worth knowing. A token's dollar value depends on two things: its price in HYPE and the price of HYPE itself. If HYPE moves, the dollar value of your tokens moves too, even if the token's HYPE price stays flat.

For step-by-step trading, read [how to buy Elysium tokens](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-buy-elysium-tokens/).

## Can you earn HYPE on Elysium?

Creators on ArkhamPad can. Every ArkhamPad coin trades in a pool with a 1% fee on every trade. 30% of those trading fees go to the coin's creator, and 70% go to ArkhamPad. Fees are collected from the pool and paid out in HYPE and in the coin itself.

How much a creator earns depends entirely on trading volume, and many coins see little volume after launch. There is no guaranteed income. The details are in [creator fees](https://arkhampad.com/learn/earn-creator-fees/).

## Can you use HYPE on Elysium without a browser wallet?

Yes. ArkhamPad lets you log in with email or Google. An embedded wallet is created for you, so there is no seed phrase to write down to get started. Trades from the embedded wallet are signed without pop-ups.

The wallet still holds real HYPE on Elysium and still needs HYPE for gas. You fund it the same ways: bridge HYPE from HyperEVM or bring USDC from Base. More on this in [trade with an email login](https://arkhampad.com/learn/trade-crypto-with-email-login/).

## How do you move HYPE back to HyperEVM?

You withdraw through the same official Elysium bridge. Withdrawals are optimistic, which means they finalize only after a challenge period. On Elysium mainnet that period is currently about 5.5 days, or around 132 hours.

Your HYPE is not lost during that time. It is waiting for the challenge window to close before it is released on HyperEVM. A faster exit route is being worked on at ArkhamPad, but there is no date yet. If you might need your HYPE on HyperEVM soon, bridge only what you plan to use on Elysium.

## FAQ

**Is HYPE on Elysium the same as HYPE on HyperEVM?**
It is the same asset, moved 1:1 through the official Elysium bridge. HYPE you deposit on HyperEVM becomes available on Elysium in the same amount. You can send it back to HyperEVM through the same bridge, although withdrawals take about 5.5 days because of the optimistic challenge period.

**How much HYPE do I need for gas on Elysium?**
Only a small amount. Gas costs on Elysium are very low, but every transaction needs some HYPE, including selling a token or bridging out. A good habit is to keep a small HYPE reserve in your wallet after every buy, so you are never stuck holding tokens you cannot sell for lack of gas.

**Can I pay with USDC instead of HYPE?**
On ArkhamPad, yes. You can bring USDC from Base, and it is converted to HYPE on the way in through a cross-chain route. You arrive on Elysium holding HYPE, which you then use for gas and trading. Tokens on Elysium are still priced and traded against HYPE.

**What is wrapped HYPE?**
Wrapped HYPE is a token-standard version of HYPE that smart contracts and liquidity pools can hold like any other token. Pools on Elysium hold wrapped HYPE. When you trade through ArkhamPad, you pay plain HYPE and receive tokens, or sell tokens and receive plain HYPE, so you do not need to wrap or unwrap it yourself.

**Why are Elysium token prices shown in HYPE?**
Most Elysium tokens are paired with HYPE in their pools, so HYPE is the natural unit for price and market cap. For example, ArkhamPad coins start at a market cap of 60 HYPE. The dollar value of any token also depends on the price of HYPE, so it can change even when the token's HYPE price does not.


# Elysium Mainnet Launch: What Traders Should Know
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-mainnet-launch/

Kinetiq announced November 9, 2026 as the public mainnet launch date for Elysium, its Layer 2 for Hyperliquid (chain ID 99901). At launch, gas is paid in HYPE, one sequencer orders transactions, and official bridge withdrawals take about 5.5 days. An upgrade that connects Elysium contracts to HyperCore market data is planned for about a month later.

## When does Elysium mainnet launch?

Kinetiq, the team behind kHYPE and the builder of Elysium, announced November 9, 2026 as the public mainnet launch date. Elysium is a Layer 2 that settles to HyperEVM, Hyperliquid's smart contract chain. If you are new to it, start with [what is Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/what-is-elysium/).

The core mainnet details:

- Chain ID: 99901
- Gas token: HYPE, bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM
- Settles to: HyperEVM (chain ID 999)
- Compatibility: full EVM, so standard wallets and Solidity contracts work

## What is live at launch, and what comes later?

Live at launch:

- Fast blocks, with a design target of 100 to 200 milliseconds, and much more block space than HyperEVM.
- HYPE as gas, with very low gas costs.
- The official Elysium bridge. Deposits arrive within seconds to a few minutes. Withdrawals take about 5.5 days.
- A single sequencer that orders transactions by priority fee, with no public mempool.
- The delayed inbox on HyperEVM, which lets users force-include a transaction if the sequencer censors it.

Planned for later:

- An ArbOS upgrade about a month after mainnet that would let smart contracts read live HyperCore market data and route orders to HyperCore.
- Permissionless fraud proofs through Arbitrum's BoLD system. Validators are permissioned at launch.

Treat planned items as plans. Build your expectations around what is live.

## Is there an Elysium airdrop or token?

No. There is no Elysium token and no official points program at this time. Gas is paid in HYPE.

Launches attract scammers. Expect fake "Elysium token" sales, fake claim pages and messages asking you to connect a wallet for an airdrop. Do not sign anything from a link you did not find through official channels.

One fee detail is public: half of Elysium sequencer fees are earmarked for open-market buybacks of KNTQ, the Kinetiq token.

## How should traders prepare for Elysium mainnet?

1. **Fund your wallet early.** Deposits arrive quickly, but you do not want to be bridging while prices move. On ArkhamPad you can bridge HYPE from HyperEVM or bring USDC from Base.
2. **Keep HYPE for gas.** Never spend your full balance on a token. You need gas to sell.
3. **Plan your exit.** Withdrawals to HyperEVM through the official bridge take about 5.5 days. Only bridge what you are ready to keep on Elysium for a while.
4. **Pick a slippage setting on purpose.** ArkhamPad offers 1%, 3%, 5% (the default) or 10%. The minimum received amount protects you if the price moves before your trade lands.
5. **Check contract addresses.** Many tokens can share the same name. On the [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/) you can search by name or contract address, and each token page shows the address and creator.

## What happens to new tokens around launch?

Expect a lot of new tokens in a short time, and most of them will be memecoins. Memecoins are highly speculative. Prices can rise and collapse within minutes, and many end close to zero. No launch period guarantees profits.

ArkhamPad's Discover page lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium from every launchpad, with market cap, 24h change, volume, buys and sells, holders and top-10 holder share. That helps you compare tokens in one place, but data is not a recommendation.

Before you buy, check a few things:

- **Holder concentration.** If a handful of wallets hold most of the supply, they can push the price down fast. See [top 10 holders](https://arkhampad.com/learn/token-holders-top-10/).
- **Liquidity.** ArkhamPad coins show an "LP locked" label because their pool liquidity can never be withdrawn. [Locked liquidity explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/locked-liquidity-explained/) covers why that matters.
- **Red flags.** Learn the common warning signs in [how to spot a rug pull](https://arkhampad.com/learn/spot-a-rug-pull/).

For a broader overview, read the [Elysium memecoins guide](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-memecoins-guide/).

## Can you launch a coin on day one?

Yes. On ArkhamPad you can [create a coin](https://arkhampad.com/create/) in about 30 seconds with a name, ticker, image and optional description and links.

Every ArkhamPad coin has a total supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens. All of it goes into the pool at launch, with no team allocation and no presale. The starting market cap is 60 HYPE for the whole supply. The pool is a Uniswap v3 style concentrated-liquidity pool against wrapped HYPE with a 1% fee on every trade, and 30% of those fees go to the creator. The liquidity is locked forever.

You can make an optional first buy in the same transaction. A launch day is busy, so plan the first hours before you start. The [memecoin launch checklist](https://arkhampad.com/learn/memecoin-launch-checklist/) walks through it.

## What trust assumptions apply at launch?

Early mainnet has more trust in the operators than it will later. One sequencer orders transactions, and validators are permissioned. Data is held by an AnyTrust-style committee that posts compact certificates to HyperEVM, with a fallback to posting full data there.

Two safeguards help. You can force-include a transaction through the delayed inbox on HyperEVM if the sequencer censors you, and withdrawals wait through a challenge period of about 5.5 days so invalid results can be disputed. Size your positions with these facts in mind.

## FAQ

**What is the Elysium mainnet launch date?**
Kinetiq announced November 9, 2026 as the public mainnet launch date for Elysium. Elysium is a Layer 2 for the Hyperliquid ecosystem that settles to HyperEVM and uses HYPE for gas. Follow Kinetiq's official channels for any change to the schedule, and be wary of unofficial posts claiming early access.

**What is the Elysium mainnet chain ID?**
The Elysium mainnet chain ID is 99901. HyperEVM, which Elysium settles to, uses chain ID 999. When adding the network to a wallet by hand, double-check the chain ID and take network details only from official sources, so you do not connect to a fake or wrong network.

**Will there be an Elysium airdrop?**
There is no Elysium token and no official points program at this time. Gas is paid in HYPE, and half of sequencer fees are earmarked for open-market KNTQ buybacks. Any site offering an Elysium token, presale or airdrop claim should be treated as a likely scam unless Kinetiq announces it officially.

**Can I withdraw from Elysium right after launch?**
Yes, through the official Elysium bridge. Withdrawals are optimistic, so they finalize only after a challenge period, currently about 5.5 days (around 132 hours) on mainnet. Deposits from HyperEVM, by contrast, arrive within seconds to a few minutes. ArkhamPad is working on a faster exit route, without a date yet.

**What is the HyperCore upgrade planned for Elysium?**
Kinetiq plans an ArbOS upgrade about a month after mainnet. It would let smart contracts on Elysium read live HyperCore market data and route orders to HyperCore, Hyperliquid's trading engine. It is not live at launch, so apps that depend on it will only work once the upgrade ships.


# Elysium Gas Fees: What a Trade Really Costs
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-gas-fees/

Elysium gas fees are paid in HYPE and are very low, so the network fee is rarely the biggest cost of a trade. The larger costs are usually the pool fee (1% on ArkhamPad coins), any router fee (0.5% for tokens launched elsewhere, none for ArkhamPad coins) and price impact. Always keep a little HYPE for gas.

## How do gas fees work on Elysium?

Gas is the fee you pay the network to process a transaction. On Elysium, gas is paid in HYPE, the same token used for gas on HyperEVM. It is taken from your wallet balance each time you buy, sell, approve a token, create a coin or bridge.

Elysium is an Arbitrum Orbit chain, so gas works the way it does on other EVM networks. A simple transfer uses less gas than a swap through a pool, and a busy network can push fees up a little. At launch, one sequencer orders transactions by priority fee, so a higher priority fee can place your transaction earlier.

You do not need a separate token for gas. If you hold HYPE on Elysium, you can pay fees. For how HYPE gets onto Elysium, read [HYPE on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/hype-on-elysium/).

## Why are Elysium gas fees so low?

Two design choices keep costs down.

- **More block space.** Hyperliquid keeps HyperEVM blocks small on purpose. Elysium was built to give trading apps, launchpads and AMMs much more room, with fast blocks and high throughput. More room means less competition for each slot.
- **Compact settlement.** Elysium does not post all its data to HyperEVM in normal operation. An AnyTrust-style committee stores the full data and posts compact certificates to HyperEVM, which keeps settlement costs small.

The result is that gas costs on Elysium are very low. Exact numbers change with demand, so check the estimate in your wallet before you confirm.

## What else do you pay when you trade on Elysium?

Gas is only one line. A full trade can include:

- **Network fee (gas).** Very low, paid in HYPE.
- **Pool fee.** Charged by the liquidity pool on every trade. ArkhamPad coins use a 1% pool fee. Tokens from other launchpads trade in pools with their own fee settings.
- **Router fee.** Trades through the ArkhamPad router of tokens launched elsewhere carry a small 0.5% fee. ArkhamPad coins pay no router fee.
- **Price impact.** The price moves against you as your trade eats into the pool. Larger trades in smaller pools pay more.
- **Token tax.** Some tokens charge their own transfer tax. Those may not be sellable through the router at all.

On ArkhamPad coins, the 1% pool fee is shared: 30% goes to the coin's creator and 70% to ArkhamPad, paid out in HYPE and in the coin.

## Example: what does a trade really cost?

Say you buy an ArkhamPad coin with 10 HYPE.

- Pool fee: 1% of the trade, about 0.1 HYPE.
- Router fee: none, because it is an ArkhamPad coin.
- Gas: a very small amount of HYPE.
- Price impact: depends on your trade size compared with the pool.

Now say you buy a token launched elsewhere with the same 10 HYPE through the ArkhamPad router. You pay the 0.5% router fee, about 0.05 HYPE, plus whatever fee that token's pool charges, plus gas and price impact.

Remember that fees apply on the way out too. A buy followed by a sell pays the pool fee twice. Before confirming, check the quote and the minimum received amount shown in the buy or sell box.

## Price impact and slippage: the costs people miss

Price impact is the move your own trade causes. Small memecoins often have thin liquidity near the current price, so a large buy can push the price up noticeably before your order completes. Comparing your trade size with the token's market cap and volume helps you judge this. [Market cap vs price](https://arkhampad.com/learn/market-cap-vs-price/) explains why market cap is the better number to watch.

Slippage tolerance is different. It is the maximum extra price change you accept between the quote and the moment your trade lands. ArkhamPad lets you choose 1%, 3%, 5% (the default) or 10%. If the price moves beyond your setting, the trade fails instead of filling at a worse price. A failed transaction still uses a little gas. [Slippage explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/slippage-explained/) covers which setting to use and when.

## How can you keep trading costs down?

- **Size trades to the pool.** Check volume and recent candles before buying. [How to read a memecoin chart](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-read-a-memecoin-chart/) shows what to look for.
- **Trade less often.** Every round trip pays pool fees twice. Frequent small flips add up.
- **Use a sensible slippage setting.** Too low and trades fail. Too high and you may fill at a poor price.
- **Watch for token taxes.** A token with its own transfer tax can cost far more than the fees above, and may be impossible to sell through the router.
- **Keep a HYPE reserve.** Running out of gas can leave you holding a token you cannot sell until you add HYPE.

For the full buy and sell flow on ArkhamPad, see [how to buy Elysium tokens](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-buy-elysium-tokens/).

## Do bridging and withdrawals cost gas?

Yes. Bridging HYPE from HyperEVM to Elysium involves a transaction on HyperEVM, which pays gas in HYPE there. Withdrawing back through the official bridge involves transactions too, and the funds finalize after a challenge period of about 5.5 days.

If you bring USDC from Base through ArkhamPad, it is converted to HYPE on the way in through a cross-chain route. The route has its own costs, so review what you will receive before you confirm.

## FAQ

**What token pays gas on Elysium?**
HYPE, Hyperliquid's native token. It is bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM through the official Elysium bridge, so you do not need a separate gas token. Gas is taken from your HYPE balance for every transaction, including buying, selling, approving tokens, creating a coin and bridging out.

**Why did my Elysium transaction fail if gas is so cheap?**
Common reasons are running out of HYPE for gas, the price moving beyond your slippage setting, or a token with its own transfer tax that the router cannot sell. Add a small amount of HYPE, try a slightly higher slippage setting, or check the token page for unusual behavior before trying again.

**Do ArkhamPad coins pay a router fee?**
No. ArkhamPad coins pay no router fee. Tokens launched elsewhere and traded through the ArkhamPad router carry a small 0.5% router fee. ArkhamPad coins do pay their 1% pool fee on every trade, which is split 30% to the coin's creator and 70% to ArkhamPad.

**Who receives the 1% pool fee on ArkhamPad coins?**
The 1% pool fee on every ArkhamPad coin trade is split between the coin's creator and ArkhamPad. The creator receives 30% and ArkhamPad receives 70%. Fees are collected from the pool and paid out in HYPE and in the coin itself, so creator earnings depend on how much the coin is traded.

**Are Elysium gas fees lower than HyperEVM gas fees?**
Elysium was built to give trading apps much more block space than HyperEVM, which keeps its blocks small on purpose, and gas costs on Elysium are very low. Exact fees on either chain change with demand, so compare the estimate your wallet shows at the time you trade rather than relying on fixed numbers.


# How to Bridge HYPE to Elysium from HyperEVM
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/bridge-hype-to-elysium/

To bridge HYPE to Elysium, hold HYPE on HyperEVM, open the official Elysium bridge (on ArkhamPad it is the Bridge page), choose HYPE, enter an amount and confirm. HYPE moves 1:1 and deposits usually arrive within seconds to a few minutes. Keep a little HYPE on Elysium afterwards, because it is also the gas token.

## What does bridging HYPE to Elysium mean?

Elysium is a Layer 2 for the Hyperliquid ecosystem, built by Kinetiq. It is a separate chain that settles to HyperEVM, so tokens do not appear on it automatically. Bridging is the process of moving HYPE from HyperEVM onto Elysium so you can use it there.

The official bridge works by locking your HYPE on HyperEVM and crediting the same amount on Elysium. The rate is 1:1: bridge 10 HYPE and you receive 10 HYPE on Elysium, minus only the small network fee for the transaction itself. No new token is created and there is nothing to swap.

If you are new to the chain, [What is Elysium?](https://arkhampad.com/learn/what-is-elysium/) covers the basics in a few minutes.

## What you need before you bridge

Check three things before you start:

- **HYPE on HyperEVM.** HyperEVM is Hyperliquid's EVM chain (chain ID 999). The bridge moves HYPE from there. If your HYPE is somewhere else, move it to your HyperEVM address first.
- **A wallet.** Any normal EVM wallet such as MetaMask works, because Elysium is fully EVM compatible. On ArkhamPad you can also log in with email or Google and get an embedded wallet created for you.
- **A little extra HYPE for gas.** The deposit transaction on HyperEVM costs a small fee in HYPE, so do not try to bridge your exact full balance.

If you do not hold HYPE at all but have USDC on Base, you can skip this guide. ArkhamPad can take USDC and convert it to HYPE on the way in, which is explained in [How to buy Elysium tokens with USDC](https://arkhampad.com/learn/buy-elysium-tokens-with-usdc/).

## How to bridge HYPE to Elysium on ArkhamPad

ArkhamPad's [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/) uses the official Elysium bridge, so you do not need a separate site. The flow is:

1. Log in to ArkhamPad with email, Google or your existing wallet.
2. Open the Bridge page.
3. Choose HYPE as the asset you want to add.
4. Enter the amount you want to move, leaving some HYPE behind on HyperEVM for the transaction fee.
5. Review the details and confirm. If you use your own wallet, approve the transaction when it asks.

That is all. Once the deposit lands, your HYPE balance on Elysium updates and you can start trading or create a coin. If you would rather see where your HYPE can go first, the [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/) lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium.

## How long does an Elysium deposit take?

Deposits from HyperEVM to Elysium usually arrive within seconds to a few minutes. The bridge has to see your transaction confirmed on HyperEVM and then credit it on Elysium, so it is not literally instant, but it is quick.

If your balance has not updated after a few minutes, check these before doing anything else:

- Confirm that the transaction actually succeeded on HyperEVM in your wallet history.
- Make sure you are looking at the same address on Elysium that sent the deposit.
- Refresh the page or reconnect your wallet so the balance is read again.

Do not send the same deposit twice just because the balance looks slow. That only moves twice the amount.

## Adding the Elysium network to your wallet

If you log in to ArkhamPad with email or Google, the embedded wallet already knows the network and you can skip this step.

If you use your own wallet, it needs the Elysium network. The mainnet chain ID is **99901**. Many apps prompt your wallet to add or switch networks automatically when you connect. If yours does not, add the network through your wallet's network settings using the details published by the Elysium team, and double-check the chain ID before you approve anything.

Because Elysium runs the standard Arbitrum Nitro stack, the wallet experience is the same as on any other EVM chain. Addresses are the same format, and your HyperEVM address is also your address on Elysium. There is no separate account to create.

## How much HYPE should you bridge?

There is no minimum that fits everyone, but two points help you decide.

First, HYPE does two jobs on Elysium. It pays for gas, and it is the currency you trade with, since tokens on ArkhamPad are paired with HYPE. When you buy a token you pay HYPE, and when you sell you receive HYPE. So bridge enough to cover the trades you plan, plus a small buffer for network fees. Gas on Elysium is very low, but a wallet with zero HYPE cannot send any transaction at all. [Elysium gas fees](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-gas-fees/) explains what a trade costs in practice.

Second, think about the way back before you bridge. Deposits are fast, but withdrawals through the official bridge are optimistic and take about 5.5 days to finalize. Bridge only what you are comfortable keeping on Elysium for at least that long. The reasons are covered in [Elysium withdrawal time](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-withdrawal-time/).

Memecoins are risky and prices can fall to near zero quickly. Only bridge an amount you can afford to lose.

## What to do after your HYPE arrives

With HYPE on Elysium you can:

- Browse every HYPE-paired token on the [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/), with market cap, volume, holders and live trades.
- Buy or sell any Elysium token from its token page, following [How to buy and sell Elysium tokens](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-buy-elysium-tokens/).
- Launch your own coin from the [create page](https://arkhampad.com/create/) in about 30 seconds.

To understand the many roles HYPE plays on the chain, read [HYPE on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/hype-on-elysium/).

## FAQ

**Is bridging HYPE to Elysium 1:1?**
Yes. The official bridge locks HYPE on HyperEVM and credits the same amount of HYPE on Elysium. You only pay the small network fee for the deposit transaction. There is no conversion, no new token and no exchange rate to worry about, because HYPE is the native gas token on both sides.

**How long does it take to bridge HYPE to Elysium?**
Deposits from HyperEVM to Elysium usually arrive within seconds to a few minutes. If your balance has not updated after that, check that the HyperEVM transaction succeeded, that you are viewing the same address on Elysium, and refresh the page before trying anything else.

**Can I bridge HYPE back from Elysium to HyperEVM quickly?**
Not through the official bridge. Withdrawals are optimistic and finalize after a challenge period of about 5.5 days, roughly 132 hours. ArkhamPad is working on a faster exit route, but there is no date for it yet, so plan for the standard withdrawal time.

**Do I need a new wallet for Elysium?**
No. Elysium is a full EVM chain, so wallets such as MetaMask work unchanged and your address is the same as on HyperEVM. You only need to add the Elysium network, chain ID 99901. If you log in to ArkhamPad with email or Google, an embedded wallet is created for you.

**What is the Elysium chain ID?**
The Elysium mainnet chain ID is 99901. HyperEVM, the chain Elysium settles to, uses chain ID 999. Always check the chain ID in your wallet before approving a network change or a bridge transaction.


# How to Buy Elysium Tokens with USDC from Base
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/buy-elysium-tokens-with-usdc/

You can buy Elysium tokens with USDC by sending USDC from Base through ArkhamPad's Bridge page. The USDC is converted to HYPE on the way in through a cross-chain route, so you arrive on Elysium holding HYPE, which you then use to buy any token. You do not need to own HYPE beforehand.

## Can you buy Elysium tokens with USDC?

Yes, with one detail worth understanding. Tokens on Elysium trade against HYPE, Hyperliquid's native token. On ArkhamPad you pay HYPE to buy a token and receive HYPE when you sell. HYPE is also the gas token that pays network fees on Elysium.

So USDC is not used directly inside a trade. Instead, ArkhamPad lets you start with USDC on Base and converts it to HYPE as it travels to Elysium. You arrive with HYPE, ready to trade, without having to buy HYPE on another platform first.

This makes USDC the easiest starting point if your stablecoins already sit on Base and you have never held HYPE.

## How the USDC route works

When you choose USDC on the Bridge page, three things happen in one flow:

- Your USDC leaves your address on Base.
- A cross-chain route carries the value over and converts it to HYPE along the way.
- HYPE lands at your address on Elysium.

You do not manage the conversion yourself and you do not need a separate account somewhere else. The result is the same as if you had bridged HYPE, which the [HYPE bridging guide](https://arkhampad.com/learn/bridge-hype-to-elysium/) describes, just with a different starting asset.

Because a conversion is involved, the amount of HYPE you receive depends on the HYPE price at that moment and on the cost of the route. Review what you will receive before you confirm.

## Step by step: from USDC on Base to your first token

1. Log in to ArkhamPad with email, Google or an existing wallet. Email and Google logins get an embedded wallet automatically, as explained in [Trade Elysium coins with just an email](https://arkhampad.com/learn/trade-crypto-with-email-login/).
2. Make sure the USDC you want to use is on Base, at the address you are using.
3. Open the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/) and choose USDC.
4. Enter the amount, review what you will receive in HYPE, and confirm.
5. Wait for HYPE to arrive on Elysium and your balance to update.
6. Find a token on the [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/) and buy it from its token page using the Buy/Sell box.

The last step is the same for everyone, whichever way they funded their wallet: open the token page, enter an amount, set slippage and confirm.

## What does it cost to use USDC?

There are a few separate costs, and it helps to keep them apart:

- **The route itself.** Moving value from Base and converting it to HYPE has a cost, which is reflected in the HYPE amount you are shown before confirming.
- **Network fees.** A transaction on Base needs a small amount of ETH for gas there. On Elysium, fees are paid in HYPE and are very low.
- **Trading fees.** Once you trade, ArkhamPad coins have a 1% pool fee and no router fee. Tokens launched elsewhere carry a small 0.5% router fee on top of their own pool fee.
- **Slippage.** The price can move between the quote and the moment your trade executes. You choose a tolerance of 1%, 3%, 5% or 10%. See [Slippage explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/slippage-explained/).

Look at the received amount at each step rather than estimating, since it already reflects the current conditions.

## USDC or HYPE: which should you start with?

Both end in the same place: HYPE on Elysium. The choice depends on what you already hold.

- **Start with HYPE** if you already have HYPE on HyperEVM. The official bridge is 1:1 and deposits arrive within seconds to a few minutes.
- **Start with USDC** if your funds are stablecoins on Base and you do not want to buy HYPE somewhere else first.

One practical point applies either way. Since you hold HYPE once you arrive, your balance moves with the HYPE price even when you are not in any trade. If you want to stay in stablecoins, that exposure is worth knowing about before you bridge. [HYPE on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/hype-on-elysium/) explains its roles on the chain.

## Getting your funds back out

Money comes back the way it is designed to: through the official Elysium bridge to HyperEVM. Withdrawals through that bridge are optimistic and take about 5.5 days to finalize. ArkhamPad is working on a faster exit route, but there is no date for it yet.

This matters for how much you bring in. Fund your wallet with an amount you are comfortable leaving on Elysium for at least a week, and read [Elysium withdrawal time](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-withdrawal-time/) before you move larger sums.

## A plain word on risk

Starting with a stablecoin does not make memecoins any safer. Most memecoins lose value, some quickly. Prices can move tens of percent within minutes, and thin pools make that worse.

Before buying, check the token's holders, its top-10 holder share and whether its liquidity is locked. ArkhamPad coins show an LP locked label, because their liquidity can never be withdrawn by anyone. For the bigger picture, read [Elysium memecoins: the complete guide](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-memecoins-guide/). Only spend what you can afford to lose.

## FAQ

**Do I need HYPE to buy tokens on Elysium?**
You need HYPE in your Elysium wallet to trade and pay gas, but you do not need to own it beforehand. On ArkhamPad you can send USDC from Base and it is converted to HYPE on the way in, so you arrive holding HYPE and can trade straight away.

**Which network does the USDC need to be on?**
ArkhamPad's USDC option takes USDC from Base. Check that your USDC is on Base and at the address you are using before you start. You will also need a small amount of ETH on Base to pay the network fee for sending it.

**Will I receive USDC on Elysium?**
No. The USDC is converted to HYPE during the transfer, so you receive HYPE on Elysium. That is what you need, because tokens on ArkhamPad trade against HYPE and network fees on Elysium are paid in HYPE.

**How much HYPE will I get for my USDC?**
It depends on the HYPE price at the time and on the cost of the cross-chain route. ArkhamPad shows the amount before you confirm, so review it at that point rather than estimating in advance. Prices move, so the figure can change between quotes.

**Can I withdraw back to USDC?**
Withdrawals from Elysium go through the official bridge to HyperEVM and take about 5.5 days to finalize. What you do with your HYPE after that is up to you. A faster exit route is being worked on, but there is no confirmed date yet.


# Elysium Withdrawal Time: Why the Bridge Takes 5.5 Days
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-withdrawal-time/

Withdrawals from Elysium to HyperEVM through the official bridge take about 5.5 days, around 132 hours. Elysium is an optimistic Layer 2, so every withdrawal waits out a challenge period during which anyone allowed to check the chain can dispute an invalid state. Deposits in the other direction arrive within seconds to a few minutes.

## How long does an Elysium withdrawal take?

On Elysium mainnet, a withdrawal through the official bridge back to HyperEVM currently takes about **5.5 days**, roughly 132 hours, before it can be finalized.

Deposits are very different. Moving HYPE from HyperEVM to Elysium usually takes seconds to a few minutes. The gap between the two directions surprises many people, so it is worth knowing the reason before you bridge funds in. The deposit flow is covered in [How to bridge HYPE to Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/bridge-hype-to-elysium/).

## Why do Elysium withdrawals take so long?

Elysium is an Arbitrum Orbit chain, which makes it an optimistic Layer 2. Optimistic means the chain does not prove every block is correct as it goes. Instead, it posts its results to HyperEVM and assumes they are correct unless someone shows otherwise.

To make that safe, there is a waiting window called the **challenge period**. During it, a validator that spots an invalid result can dispute it, and the dispute is settled on HyperEVM. Only after the window closes without a successful challenge is the result treated as final.

A withdrawal is a claim that you own funds on Elysium and want them released on HyperEVM. That claim can only be honored once the state it depends on is final. So every withdrawal through the official bridge waits for the challenge period, whatever its size.

Deposits do not need this wait. They start on HyperEVM, which is already final, so Elysium can credit them almost right away. [Elysium vs HyperEVM](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-vs-hyperevm/) explains how the two chains relate.

## Who checks the chain during the challenge period?

At launch, Elysium's validators are permissioned, meaning a known set of parties run them. Permissionless fraud proofs, using Arbitrum's BoLD system, are planned for later. With BoLD, anyone would be able to challenge an invalid state, which strengthens the security model the waiting period is there to support.

Elysium also has one sequencer at launch. The sequencer orders transactions by priority fee, and there is no public mempool. If the sequencer ever refused to include your transaction, you can force-include it through the delayed inbox on HyperEVM. That path matters for withdrawals in particular, because it means a withdrawal cannot simply be blocked forever by the sequencer.

For more on how the chain is built and run, read [What is Elysium?](https://arkhampad.com/learn/what-is-elysium/).

## What happens during a withdrawal, step by step

In broad terms, an official bridge withdrawal goes through these stages:

1. You start the withdrawal on Elysium. Your HYPE leaves your Elysium balance.
2. The withdrawal is included in a batch that is posted to HyperEVM.
3. The challenge period runs, currently about 5.5 days.
4. Once it ends, the withdrawal can be finalized and the HYPE is released on HyperEVM.

During the wait, the funds are in neither balance you can spend from. They are not lost, they are in transit. Keep a record of the transaction so you can follow it.

## Is there a faster way to withdraw from Elysium?

Not through the official bridge. The challenge period is part of how an optimistic Layer 2 stays secure, so it is not something an app can switch off.

ArkhamPad is working on a faster exit route for its users. There is no release date yet, so do not plan around it. Until it is live, treat 5.5 days as the time it takes to get funds back to HyperEVM.

Be careful with anyone offering instant withdrawals through unknown sites or direct messages. Scams often target people who are waiting for funds. Only use bridges you have verified, and never share a seed phrase.

## How to plan around the withdrawal time

A few habits make the waiting period much less of a problem:

- **Bridge in what you are comfortable leaving on Elysium for at least a week.** Fast deposits make it easy to forget the exit takes days.
- **Do not count on exiting fast in a hurry.** If you need funds by a specific date, start the withdrawal well before it.
- **Keep some HYPE on Elysium.** HYPE pays gas, and starting a withdrawal is itself a transaction.
- **Stay on-chain if you are still trading.** Selling a token for HYPE on Elysium is quick. Only the bridge back to HyperEVM is slow.

The timing is also one reason why liquidity locks matter on Elysium. On ArkhamPad coins, liquidity is held by the launcher contract and cannot be withdrawn by anyone, as explained in [Locked liquidity explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/locked-liquidity-explained/).

## Will the withdrawal time change after mainnet?

The 5.5 day figure is the current challenge period on Elysium mainnet. Kinetiq has announced the public mainnet launch for November 9, 2026, and further upgrades are planned, including permissionless fraud proofs later on. Any change to the withdrawal window would be announced by the Elysium team, so treat 5.5 days as the working number until then. [Elysium mainnet launch](https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-mainnet-launch/) covers what else traders should know about the launch.

## FAQ

**How long does it take to withdraw from Elysium to HyperEVM?**
About 5.5 days, roughly 132 hours, through the official bridge. Elysium is an optimistic Layer 2, so every withdrawal waits out a challenge period before it is finalized on HyperEVM. The wait is the same regardless of the amount you withdraw.

**Why are deposits to Elysium fast but withdrawals slow?**
Deposits start on HyperEVM, which is already final, so Elysium can credit them within seconds to a few minutes. Withdrawals depend on Elysium's state, which only becomes final on HyperEVM after the challenge period ends without a successful dispute. That waiting window is what makes optimistic rollups secure.

**Can I cancel or speed up an Elysium withdrawal?**
Through the official bridge, the challenge period cannot be skipped. ArkhamPad is working on a faster exit route for its users, but it has no release date yet. Be cautious of anyone offering instant withdrawals through unverified sites or private messages.

**Are my funds safe during the withdrawal period?**
Your funds are in transit, not lost. If the sequencer ever refused to include a transaction, users can force-include it through the delayed inbox on HyperEVM. Validators are permissioned at launch, with permissionless fraud proofs planned for later. As with any bridge, some technical risk always remains.

**Can I still trade while a withdrawal is pending?**
Yes, with the HYPE that remains in your Elysium wallet. The amount being withdrawn has already left your Elysium balance, so it cannot be used for trades. Keep some HYPE on Elysium for gas and any trades you still plan to make.


# Trade Crypto with Email Login: Elysium Coins Made Simple
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/trade-crypto-with-email-login/

On ArkhamPad you can trade Elysium coins by logging in with just an email address or a Google account. An embedded wallet is created for you, so there is no seed phrase to write down to get started, and trades are signed without wallet pop-ups. You fund it with HYPE or USDC and trade like any other user.

## Can you really trade crypto with just an email?

Yes. On ArkhamPad, logging in with an email address or a Google account creates an **embedded wallet** for you. It is a real on-chain wallet with its own address on Elysium. It simply lives inside the app instead of in a browser extension you had to install yourself.

From there, everything works the same as with any wallet: you fund it, buy and sell tokens, and launch coins. People who already use a wallet such as MetaMask can still connect it instead. Both options reach the same tokens and the same prices.

## How the embedded wallet works

Traditional crypto wallets ask you to install software, write down a seed phrase (a list of recovery words) and approve every action in a pop-up. That is a lot of steps before a first trade.

With an email or Google login on ArkhamPad:

- The wallet is created automatically when you log in.
- There is no seed phrase to write down to get started.
- Trades from the embedded wallet are signed without pop-ups, so a buy or sell goes through after you confirm in the app.

The wallet has a normal address, so you can receive funds to it and see its activity on-chain like any other.

## Funding an email wallet

A new wallet starts empty. You add funds from the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/) in one of two ways:

- **HYPE from HyperEVM.** The official Elysium bridge moves HYPE 1:1 and deposits usually arrive within seconds to a few minutes. See [How to bridge HYPE to Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/bridge-hype-to-elysium/).
- **USDC from Base.** USDC is converted to HYPE on the way in, so you arrive holding HYPE. See [How to buy Elysium tokens with USDC](https://arkhampad.com/learn/buy-elysium-tokens-with-usdc/).

Either way you end up with HYPE on Elysium. HYPE is the currency tokens trade against on ArkhamPad and also pays the network fee, so keep a little spare for gas.

## Making your first trade

Once funded, trading takes a few steps:

1. Find a token on the [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/), which lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium. Search by name or contract address.
2. Open the token page and check its chart, holders and recent trades.
3. In the Buy/Sell box, enter how much HYPE to spend.
4. Choose a slippage tolerance, then confirm.

Because the embedded wallet signs without pop-ups, confirming in the app is the final step. That speed is useful on fast-moving tokens, but it also means you should read the quote carefully before you confirm. The full flow, including selling, is in [How to buy and sell Elysium tokens](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-buy-elysium-tokens/).

## Launching a coin with an email login

The same login also works for creating a coin. You choose a name, ticker and image, add an optional description and links, and can make an optional first buy. The whole process takes about 30 seconds on the [create page](https://arkhampad.com/create/), and [How to create a token on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/create-a-token-on-elysium/) walks through each field.

Every ArkhamPad coin launches with a total supply of 1,000,000,000 tokens, all of it placed in the pool, and its liquidity is locked forever. As the creator, you receive 30% of the trading fees on your coin, paid to your wallet in HYPE and in the coin. [Earn creator fees](https://arkhampad.com/learn/earn-creator-fees/) explains how that works, and the [memecoin launch checklist](https://arkhampad.com/learn/memecoin-launch-checklist/) covers your first day after launch.

## Email wallet or your own wallet: which to use?

Both are valid. The difference is mostly about convenience and how you prefer to manage keys.

- **Email or Google login** suits people who are new to crypto, want to try Elysium quickly, or trade often and do not want a pop-up for every action.
- **An existing wallet** suits people who already hold funds in it, use it across many apps, or prefer to control their keys through software they chose themselves.

Some people use both: a familiar wallet for long-term holdings and an email login for quick trading with a smaller balance.

## Keeping an email wallet safe

An email login is only as secure as the email or Google account behind it. A few simple habits go a long way:

- Turn on two-factor authentication for that email or Google account.
- Use a strong, unique password that you do not reuse elsewhere.
- Never share login codes with anyone, including people claiming to be support.
- Keep only the amount you are actively trading in a hot wallet like this.

Remember too that memecoins are risky whatever wallet you use. Most lose value, and prices can drop sharply within minutes. Only trade with money you can afford to lose.

## FAQ

**Do I need MetaMask to trade on Elysium?**
No. On ArkhamPad you can log in with an email address or a Google account and an embedded wallet is created for you. If you already use MetaMask or another EVM wallet, you can connect it instead. Both options trade the same tokens at the same prices.

**Is there a seed phrase with an email login?**
There is no seed phrase to write down to get started. The embedded wallet is created when you log in, and you access it through your email or Google account. That is why securing that account with a strong password and two-factor authentication matters.

**Why are there no wallet pop-ups when I trade?**
Trades from ArkhamPad's embedded wallet are signed without pop-ups. You review the quote and confirm in the app, and the transaction is sent. This makes trading faster, so read the amount, slippage and minimum received carefully before you confirm.

**How do I add money to an email wallet?**
Use the Bridge page. You can bridge HYPE from HyperEVM through the official Elysium bridge, or send USDC from Base, which is converted to HYPE on the way in. Either way you arrive holding HYPE, which you use for trades and gas.

**Can I create a coin with an email login?**
Yes. The same login works on the create page. Choose a name, ticker and image, add optional details and an optional first buy. It takes about 30 seconds, and as the creator you receive 30% of the trading fees on your coin.


# How to Buy Elysium Tokens and Sell Them (Step by Step)
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-buy-elysium-tokens/

To buy an Elysium token, fund your wallet with HYPE, open the token's page on ArkhamPad, enter how much HYPE to spend in the Buy/Sell box, choose a slippage tolerance and confirm. Selling is the same in reverse: you enter the token amount and receive HYPE. ArkhamPad's router can trade any Elysium token from one page.

## What you need before you buy

Every token on ArkhamPad trades against HYPE, Hyperliquid's native token. You pay HYPE to buy and receive HYPE when you sell. HYPE also pays the network fee on Elysium. So the one thing you need is HYPE in your Elysium wallet.

- Log in with email, Google or an existing wallet. Email and Google logins get an embedded wallet automatically.
- Add HYPE through the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/), either by bridging HYPE from HyperEVM or by sending USDC from Base, which arrives as HYPE.
- Keep a little HYPE aside for gas so you can still sell later.

## Finding the right token

The [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/) lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium, from every launchpad. For each token you can see market cap, 24h change, volume, buys and sells, holders, top-10 holder share and live trades.

If you know which token you want, search by its name or contract address. Names and tickers can be copied by anyone, so the **contract address** is the reliable way to be sure you have the right token. Get it from a source you trust and compare it to the one shown on the token page.

On the token page, look at the chart, the holders list and the recent trades before you buy. [How to read a memecoin chart](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-read-a-memecoin-chart/) and [Market cap vs price](https://arkhampad.com/learn/market-cap-vs-price/) explain what those numbers tell you.

## How to buy an Elysium token step by step

1. Open the token page.
2. In the Buy/Sell box, choose Buy.
3. Enter the amount of HYPE you want to spend.
4. Read the quote: how many tokens you are expected to receive and the minimum you will accept.
5. Choose your slippage tolerance: 1%, 3%, 5% (the default) or 10%.
6. Confirm. With your own wallet, approve the transaction when it asks. With an embedded wallet, it is signed without a pop-up.

When the trade completes, the tokens appear in your wallet and your trade shows in the live trades list.

## How to sell an Elysium token

Selling uses the same box:

1. Open the token page.
2. In the Buy/Sell box, choose Sell.
3. Enter how many tokens you want to sell.
4. Check the quote for the HYPE you will receive and the minimum received.
5. Choose slippage and confirm.

The HYPE lands in your Elysium wallet. From there you can buy another token, or bridge back to HyperEVM, which takes about 5.5 days through the official bridge.

## How ArkhamPad routes your trade

Tokens on Elysium do not all live in the same kind of pool. Some use Uniswap v3 style pools and some use v4 style pools. ArkhamPad's router is a single smart contract that can trade both, so you can buy or sell any Elysium token from one page without looking up where its liquidity sits.

Fees work like this:

- **ArkhamPad coins** pay the 1% pool fee on each trade and **no router fee**.
- **Tokens launched elsewhere** carry a small 0.5% router fee, in addition to whatever fee their own pool charges.
- **Network fees** are paid in HYPE and are very low on Elysium.

One exception to know about: some tokens charge their own transfer tax, taking a cut every time they move. Those tokens may not be sellable through the router. If a sell keeps failing, a transfer tax is one possible reason, and it is a good reason to check a token's details before you buy.

## Choosing slippage and reading minimum received

Slippage is the difference between the price you are quoted and the price you actually get. On a busy memecoin, other trades can land just before yours and move the price.

Your slippage setting is the most you will accept. The quote turns it into a **minimum received**: if the trade would give you less than that, it fails instead of filling at a worse price. A failed trade still uses a small amount of gas, but your HYPE or tokens stay in your wallet.

- **1% to 3%** suits calmer tokens with deeper pools.
- **5%**, the default, is a reasonable middle for most memecoins.
- **10%** may be needed in very fast markets, but you accept a worse fill.

[Slippage explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/slippage-explained/) goes deeper on what to set and why trades fail.

## Checks before you press confirm

Memecoins are risky. Most lose value, and prices can fall sharply in minutes. A quick check before buying helps you avoid the worst cases:

- **Liquidity.** ArkhamPad coins show an LP locked label, meaning the pool can never be withdrawn by anyone. Tokens from elsewhere may not offer that. See [Locked liquidity explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/locked-liquidity-explained/).
- **Holder concentration.** A very high top-10 holder share means a few wallets could sell heavily. See [Token holders and top-10 concentration](https://arkhampad.com/learn/token-holders-top-10/).
- **Trading pattern.** Look at buys versus sells and the live trades list for unusual activity.

[How to spot a rug pull](https://arkhampad.com/learn/spot-a-rug-pull/) lists more warning signs. Nothing here is financial advice. Only spend what you can afford to lose.

## FAQ

**What do I pay with when buying Elysium tokens?**
You pay with HYPE. Every token on ArkhamPad trades against HYPE, and HYPE also pays the network fee. If you only hold USDC on Base, you can send it through the Bridge page and it is converted to HYPE on the way in.

**Can I buy tokens that were not launched on ArkhamPad?**
Yes. ArkhamPad's router trades both Uniswap v3 style and v4 style pools, so you can buy or sell any HYPE-paired Elysium token from its token page. Tokens launched elsewhere carry a small 0.5% router fee. ArkhamPad coins pay no router fee.

**What slippage should I use?**
The default is 5%, a reasonable middle for most memecoins. Use 1% to 3% for calmer tokens with deeper pools, and 10% only in very fast markets where trades keep failing. Higher slippage makes a fill more likely but can give you a worse price.

**Why did my trade fail?**
Usually the price moved beyond your slippage setting, so the trade would have returned less than your minimum received and was cancelled. Try again or raise slippage slightly. Other causes include not enough HYPE for gas, or a token with its own transfer tax.

**Why can't I sell a token?**
Some tokens charge their own transfer tax on every transfer, and those may not be sellable through the ArkhamPad router. Also check that you have a little HYPE left for gas. If a sell keeps failing, check the token's details or contact its creator.

**How do I make sure I am buying the right token?**
Search by contract address rather than name, since names and tickers can be copied. Get the address from a source you trust and compare it with the one shown on the token page before you buy.


# Elysium Memecoins: The Complete Guide
URL: https://arkhampad.com/learn/elysium-memecoins-guide/

Elysium memecoins are community tokens launched on Elysium, Kinetiq's Layer 2 for the Hyperliquid ecosystem, and traded against HYPE. You can find every HYPE-paired Elysium token on ArkhamPad's Discover page and buy or sell it from one token page. Memecoins are highly speculative, so only trade money you can afford to lose.

## What are Elysium memecoins?

A memecoin is a token whose value comes mostly from attention, community and culture rather than from cash flows or a product. Most start as a joke, a mascot or a running theme on social media. Their prices can rise or fall by large amounts in minutes.

Elysium memecoins are memecoins that live on [Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/what-is-elysium/), a Layer 2 network for the Hyperliquid ecosystem built by Kinetiq. Almost all of them trade in pools paired with HYPE, Hyperliquid's native token. You buy them with HYPE and receive HYPE when you sell.

Because Elysium is a full EVM chain, these are standard EVM tokens that work with normal EVM wallets and tools.

## Why are memecoins launching on Elysium?

Memecoin trading creates a lot of small, fast transactions. Hyperliquid deliberately keeps HyperEVM blocks small, so busy trading apps compete for limited space there. Elysium was built to give trading apps, launchpads and AMMs (automated market makers, the pools that let you swap tokens without an order book) much more block space.

A few design choices matter for traders:

- **Fast blocks.** Elysium targets blocks of roughly 100 to 200 milliseconds, so trades confirm quickly.
- **HYPE for gas.** Network fees are paid in HYPE bridged 1:1 from HyperEVM. There is no separate gas token to buy.
- **Low fees.** Gas costs are very low, which matters when you make many small trades.
- **Settlement to HyperEVM.** Elysium is an Arbitrum Orbit chain that settles to HyperEVM, so it stays connected to the wider Hyperliquid ecosystem.

Kinetiq has announced November 9, 2026 as the public mainnet launch date. For more on how HYPE moves between the two networks, see [HYPE on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/hype-on-elysium/).

## Where can you find every Elysium memecoin?

New tokens appear on Elysium from several launchpads. ArkhamPad's [Discover page](https://arkhampad.com/) lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium from every launchpad in one place. That is hundreds of tokens, not only those launched on ArkhamPad.

For each token, Discover shows:

- Market cap and 24-hour price change
- Trading volume and the number of buys and sells
- Holder count and the share of supply held by the top 10 wallets
- Live trades as they happen

You can search by name or paste a contract address. Searching by address is the safest way to find a specific coin, because anyone can create a token with the same name or ticker as a popular one.

## How does a coin launched on ArkhamPad work?

Coins created on ArkhamPad follow one fixed setup, which makes them easier to compare:

- **Supply:** 1,000,000,000 tokens per coin.
- **Fair start:** the entire supply goes into the trading pool at launch. There is no team allocation and no presale. The creator may make an optional first buy in the same transaction, paid through the pool like any other buy.
- **Starting market cap:** 60 HYPE for the whole supply.
- **Pool:** a Uniswap v3 style concentrated-liquidity pool against wrapped HYPE, with a 1% pool fee on every trade.
- **Fees:** 30% of trading fees go to the coin's creator and 70% to ArkhamPad.
- **Locked liquidity:** the pool position is held by the launcher contract and cannot be withdrawn by anyone, including the creator and ArkhamPad.

A common way people lose money on memecoins is a liquidity rug pull, where the creator removes the pool's funds and leaves holders with tokens they cannot sell. That is not possible on ArkhamPad coins, which carry an LP locked label on Discover. [Locked liquidity explained](https://arkhampad.com/learn/locked-liquidity-explained/) covers how this works. Locked liquidity does not stop the price from falling, though. Holders can still sell, and the price can still drop sharply.

## How do you buy an Elysium memecoin?

You can trade any Elysium token from its ArkhamPad token page, including tokens launched elsewhere.

1. Log in with email, Google or an existing wallet. Email and Google users get an embedded wallet created automatically.
2. Add funds. Bridge HYPE from HyperEVM on the [Bridge page](https://arkhampad.com/bridge/), or send USDC from Base, which arrives as HYPE on Elysium.
3. Open the token from Discover and check its contract address.
4. Enter an amount of HYPE, review the quote and the minimum you will receive, and confirm.

Keep a little HYPE in your balance for network fees. Tokens launched on other launchpads carry a 0.5% router fee; ArkhamPad coins pay no router fee. The full walkthrough is in [how to buy and sell Elysium tokens](https://arkhampad.com/learn/how-to-buy-elysium-tokens/).

## What should you check before buying a memecoin?

A minute of checking can save you from the most common mistakes:

- **Contract address.** Confirm it matches the one the project shares. Copycat tokens are common.
- **Liquidity status.** Look for the LP locked label, or find out how the pool is held for tokens from elsewhere.
- **Top-10 holder share.** If a handful of wallets hold most of the supply, a few sellers can crash the price.
- **Buys versus sells and volume.** Real activity from many traders is a better sign than a few large trades.
- **Age.** Very new tokens move fastest and carry the most risk.
- **Transfer tax.** Some tokens charge their own tax on transfers, and these may not be sellable through the router.

For a longer list of warning signs, read [how to spot a rug pull](https://arkhampad.com/learn/spot-a-rug-pull/).

## What are the risks of Elysium memecoins?

Memecoins are among the riskiest assets in crypto. Most lose most of their value, and many go to zero. Treat any money you put into memecoins as money you are prepared to lose entirely.

There are also risks specific to a new network. Elysium mainnet is new. At launch, one sequencer orders transactions and validators are permissioned, with permissionless fraud proofs planned for later. Withdrawals through the official bridge back to HyperEVM take about 5.5 days, so you cannot move funds out instantly. Plan for that before you deposit.

Nothing on ArkhamPad is financial advice. A locked pool, a high holder count or a rising chart does not mean a coin will go up.

## Can you launch your own Elysium memecoin?

Yes. On ArkhamPad you can [create a coin](https://arkhampad.com/create/) with a name, ticker, image and an optional description and links. It takes about 30 seconds, and you can add an optional first buy in the same transaction. As the creator, you earn 30% of the trading fees your coin generates, paid out in HYPE and in the coin. Step-by-step instructions are in [how to create a token on Elysium](https://arkhampad.com/learn/create-a-token-on-elysium/).

## FAQ

**Do I need HYPE to buy Elysium memecoins?**
Yes, in practice. Elysium memecoins trade in pools paired with HYPE, and network fees on Elysium are paid in HYPE. On ArkhamPad you can bridge HYPE from HyperEVM, or send USDC from Base, which is converted to HYPE on the way in. Keep a small amount of HYPE aside for gas so you can still sell later.

**Is there an Elysium token or airdrop?**
There is no Elysium token and no official points program at this time. Be careful with anyone claiming to sell or airdrop an Elysium token. Half of Elysium sequencer fees are earmarked for open-market buybacks of KNTQ, the Kinetiq token, but that is separate from any memecoin you trade on the network.

**Can I trade Elysium tokens that were not launched on ArkhamPad?**
Yes. ArkhamPad's Discover page lists every HYPE-paired token on Elysium from every launchpad, and you can trade any of them from its token page through the ArkhamPad router.
